items.stem: What is the role of the data plane in a service mesh?

options.text: The sidecar proxies that intercept and handle service-to-service traffic
options.rationale: Correct: the data plane carries the actual request traffic.

options.text: The component that stores configuration and pushes policy

options.rationale: The data plane is the mesh's proxies, not just the gateway.
The mesh does not manage databases.

items.explanation: Correct: the data plane carries the actual request traffic.

items.stem: What does enabling mutual TLS (mTLS) in a mesh provide?

options.text: Encrypted and mutually authenticated service-to-service communication
options.rationale: Correct: mTLS authenticates both ends and encrypts traffic between workloads.

options.text: Authentication of the human end user
options.rationale: mTLS authenticates workloads, not end users.

items.stem: Which statements about service-mesh traffic management are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Traffic splitting lets you send a small percentage to a canary version
options.rationale: Correct: gradual rollout reduces blast radius.

options.text: Timeouts and retries can be configured at the mesh without app changes
options.rationale: Correct: resilience policy lives in the mesh.

options.text: A mesh removes all latency from requests
Retries can never worsen an outage
options.rationale: False; aggressive retries can amplify load.
